kind: score-only: pooled net-subsumption strength for RQ2, selection (mrs-nsga2-apportion against mrs-weighted) and grading (mrs-nsga2-apportion against aurus-nsga2-apportion)
kind_note: No search ran. Each side's pool is the union of its 30 rematch runs' last-cut frontiers (separation-recount-rematch-s0 sidecars, tlsf_prc.frontier), with members whose bodies match once comments and whitespace are removed merged into one node (hash_bodies.py). Within each side every prefilter-surviving node pair is compared, giving the pooled frontier as classes of undominated nodes; every Pareto node is compared with every scalarised and ladder node that survives the fingerprint prefilter. 23 families are scored exactly. humanoid-531 and humanoid-742 are estimated from the first 100 draws a side of a seeded permutation (scripts/pooled.py, sample-plan and sample-score). The pass ran as one pre-planned pair list per host through campaign.py's compare phase; pairs already decided were left out of the lists and their rows come from the earlier runs below.
registration: PLAN.md of the paper repository (benmandrew/counter-paper), commit decdc10 of 2026-10-06 15:10, which changed strength to the pooled design. There is no PLAN.md in this directory.

pair_lists.build: scripts/pooled.py cross-pools (pairs-crosspool.csv) and sample-plan for batches 1-4 at 20 draws a side, joined with stage-1 pairs-within (s1/all.csv) and sample batch 0, both orders of each id checked against every earlier result, shuffled with seed 20261006 and dealt round-robin to av1, av2, av3. The joining script ran inline and was not saved; the pair lists' md5s are recorded per host.

av3.note: Attempt 1 at 22:15:03 failed in staging: cmake --build stopped on a missing zstd depend rule in the build tree left by campaign/fretish-mixed. The 22:20 tick found the checkout already at 0fd968f and ran the phase without rebuilding, so the binary is the e04317d build left from 2026-10-01-fretish-mixed (the manifest records commit e04317d, dirty 0). git diff e04317d 0fd968f touches nothing under src/, third_party/, cmake/ or CMakeLists.txt, so the source is the one the other two hosts built. The skipped rebuild after a failed staging is a campaign.py defect, not fixed here.

hand_run.what: The start of this pass, run by hand through scripts/q.sh and scripts/drive.py before the move to campaign.py, which breaks the rule against hand-rolled ssh launches. Stage-1 chunk 00 and part of sample batch 0 ran on each host from 2026-10-06 21:06 until the queues and their compare processes were killed at about 22:05; rows written before the kill are kept.

per_run_pass.what: The superseded per-run subsumption pass of 2026-10-06 (scripts/plan.py, scripts/run.py), whose pair ids use the same spec|label@seed|file|label@seed|file form, so any pair it decided answers the pooled pass.

scoring.inputs: the 12 result files above: six per-run, three hand-run, three campaign

steps.result: 30,671 frontier classes over the 23 exact families (out/classes.csv); pairs-cross.csv empty, so every cross pair between classes has a row
out/sample/estimates.csv; prints open, since one half-width exceeds HALF = 0.10

result.test: exact Wilcoxon signed-rank over families, zeros dropped; net is sub(B by A) - sub(A by B), positive when A is the stronger
result.sampled_half_widths: 95% half-widths at 100 draws are 0.043-0.118; humanoid-531's sub(Pareto by scalarised) at 0.118 misses the 0.10 target. Dropping both sampled families leaves both conclusions.
caveats: Pooling favours the side with more frontier classes. The scalarised frontier is the larger in 22 of the 23 exact families, and the Pareto arm's one win, full-arbiter-aurus, is the one where its frontier is the larger; within families the net share does not track the size ratio (Spearman 0.06, p 0.78). The per-run matched design gave the same direction (-0.026).
In grading the ladder frontier is the larger in 5 of the 23 exact families, and MRS is the stronger on 3 of those 5.
No equal-time strength pass was run; the scalarised arm's runs are longer.
